analysis: Reviewed the LaunchAgent.swift base and head and the test patch. The only functional change in LaunchAgent.swift is two new keys, EngineV2Factory.prefillChunkKey and EngineV2Factory.stepTokenBudgetKey, added to inferencePassthroughEnvKeys (head lines 302-305), plus doc comments. passthroughEnvironment (head 351-372) forwards only allowlisted, non-empty values from the installing shell into the plist EnvironmentVariables. The new keys carry scheduler prefill geometry (chunk size and step token budget), which are performance and rollback knobs. They are not secrets, do not touch the attestation, App Attest, or key-custody paths, and do not affect the cache scope, TTL, or HMAC lookup posture of T-041. The operator already controls this environment, which is within ADV-001's capability and was already true for the other tuning keys. The allowlist stays bounded, and the worker opt-in is still emitted only when it is exactly 1. Stop, disable, bootout, and watchdog semantics (KeepAlive=false, RunAtLoad=true, launchctl disable on stop) are unchanged between base and head. The test file change is benchmark report schema v5, adding optional prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep, with backward-compatible decode of schema 4. It has no security surface. Unverified: how EngineV2Factory parses the new env values, for example bounds on chunk size or step tokens that could drive memory exhaustion (a T-029/availability concern). That code is outside the supplied evidence and an operator-chosen value is self-inflicted, so I record this as an integration question and not a finding. No regression identified in these units.
